touches.text: A retirement checks its callers in the same act as the deletion: nothing imports the module being deleted, and nothing runs the command or path being deleted. A file that only names it (a fixture, a record, a charter) is not a caller. Nothing checks afterwards. Why? Naming is history; only a caller breaks, and a caller that comes later breaks loudly on its own. A standing proof that a thing stays gone is history kept as code.

`cairn codemother retire <path>...` does the deletion. It runs the proofs of the files that name the target, before and after moving it aside. A proof that turns red is a caller, and the target goes back. Why? Running a proof tells a caller from a mention; reading the text cannot.

Lifetimes. Each tree declares its lifetime when it is made: kept, one activity (eg one sleep run), or until its source file changes. Dropping a tree drops its leaves and its own links. A node goes only when no tree indexes it, so whatever a temporary tree's activity promoted into a permanent tree outlives it. The drop is enforced, not a habit. WHY: a run that ends without dropping its tables leaves them behind forever.

Commit: the proofs of the component the ticket changed, since RULE 1 bounds a change to its component. Passing them puts the component in service, yellow: proven where it changed, not yet measured against what depends on it. In service needs only the best we can do now: 80% trust.
VERBS: run, notices, CodeMother's verbs reached over the bus (RULE 1). COMMANDS: cairn codemother test (--hollow, --seal, --exec, ...), shortcut cairn test; proofgate (the hook: proofs run by hand).
scratch: a proof's throwaway temp dirs and worktrees, cleaned up by the door. WHY: a run must leave nothing behind (4.3.1.7). USERS: the tester.
